outcome: Early-onset Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) incidence in young children
cohort: Participants included 632 incident cases of T1D among children under 10 years old, identified from 1,478,573 live births in Taiwan between 2000-2005, with 10 matched controls per case.
finding: The study found that childhood infection, younger maternal age, older paternal age, maternal Caesarean section, maternal gestational diabetes mellitus, and paternal type 1 or type 2 diabetes were significantly associated with an increased risk of early-onset type 1 diabetes in young children.
mod_finding: Mothers with Caesarean section (CS) were found to have an increased risk of offspring developing T1D (OR = 2.35, 95% CI = 1.52-3.64).
